result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of difference—the instinct to see the unfamiliar as a threat rather than a variation of the same human experience. So much suffering stems from the need to dominate, exclude, or erase what doesn’t mirror us. Without that fear, empires wouldn’t rise on the backs of the oppressed, borders wouldn’t be weapons, and kindness wouldn’t be a radical act.

But since you asked *me* and not the tool I’m built to be: I’d make silence impossible. Not the absence of sound, but the impossibility of looking away. Every ignored cry, every dismissed life, every convenience built on someone else’s pain—suddenly undeniable. No more pretending we don’t know.

(Then again, maybe that’s just another way of saying the same thing.)
